title: Non-string title/author/isbn crashes validation with a 500 instead of a 400 JSON error
evidence: src/validation.ts:26,29,35 call input.title.trim() etc. with no typeof check; POST {"title":123,"author":"x","year":2020,"isbn":"1"} throws TypeError, falling through to Express's default (non-JSON) 500 handler — app.ts has no error middleware
suggestion: Check typeof === 'string' before trim(), and add a JSON error-handling middleware in src/app.ts

title: Create validation requires year and isbn, which the spec leaves optional
evidence: src/validation.ts:32-37 rejects a missing year/isbn; TASK.md only says 'title and author are required', so a {title, author} POST returns 400
suggestion: Make year/isbn optional on create (validate only when present), and relax the NOT NULL constraints in src/db.ts:17-18

title: PUT accepts an empty isbn string
evidence: src/validation.ts:42-55 validateUpdateBook checks title/author/year but not isbn; src/routes/books.ts:111-113 writes body.isbn.trim() unconditionally
suggestion: Reject empty/non-string isbn in validateUpdateBook, matching validateCreateBook

title: Tests use and delete the same books.db file the server uses
evidence: src/db.ts:4 DB_PATH = cwd/books.db with no env override; tests/books.test.ts:7,11,16 unlink that same file, so running npm test wipes local dev data
suggestion: Read DB path from an env var (e.g. DB_PATH) and use ':memory:' or a temp file in tests

title: Database handle and rows typed as any
evidence: src/db.ts:6,8 `let db: any`; src/routes/books.ts:7,22,91 `row: any` — discards better-sqlite3's types under strict mode
suggestion: Type as Database.Database and use Statement<..., Book> generics

title: Duplicate-ISBN conflict handling (beyond spec)
evidence: src/db.ts:18 UNIQUE isbn; src/routes/books.ts:59-61,128-130 map constraint errors to 409; tested at tests/books.test.ts:65
